workflow: Restate the requirements and list states, entities, and invariants yourself before touching the AI.
Sketch the classes and interfaces by hand: who owns which state, and which methods change it.
Ask the AI for boilerplate only: enums, dataclasses, test scaffolding.
Review every generated block out loud: thread safety, single responsibility, missing states, edge cases, leaked internals.
Run the reference tests, then probe invalid input, concurrency, and state ownership. Built-in tests are examples, not proof that every requirement is covered.
Close with trade-offs and what you would change at scale.

pattern_cards.name: Strategy
pattern_cards.when: Several interchangeable algorithms behind one interface, chosen at runtime.
pitfalls: Do not add a Strategy for a single implementation.

pattern_cards.name: Observer
pattern_cards.when: Other parts of the system react to events without the publisher knowing them.
pitfalls: Do not call listeners while holding a lock.

pattern_cards.name: State
pattern_cards.when: Behavior depends on a status with strict allowed moves.
pitfalls: A class per state only pays off when states carry lots of behavior.

pattern_cards.name: Factory
pattern_cards.when: Callers need an object but should not know which class or how it is built.
pitfalls: Creation on first use must be thread-safe.
Skip it when a constructor is enough.

pattern_cards.name: Builder
pattern_cards.when: An object has many optional parts and must be valid when finished.
pitfalls: In Python, keyword arguments and dataclasses often replace it.
Validate in build(), not in every setter.

pattern_cards.name: Locks and concurrent maps
pattern_cards.when: Shared mutable state touched by several threads.
pattern_cards.sketch:
with self._lock:  # check and act together
    current = self._state.get(key)
    if allowed(current, target):
        self._state[key] = target
# do slow work (I/O, callbacks) outside the lock
pitfalls: Check-then-act races are the classic bug.
Never call out to unknown code while holding a lock.
Start with one lock; shard by key when contention shows up.
In Python, the GIL does not make compound operations atomic.

problems.title: Workflow step state-transition logger
problems.prompt: Design a component that logs state transitions for steps in a workflow engine. This reconstructed practice prompt came from the existing prep notes; the original report is not linked, so treat it as a drill rather than a prediction of your onsite question.
requirements: Record every state change of a workflow step: who, when, from, to, and why.
Reject illegal transitions, such as moving a finished step back to running.
Query the full history and the current state of any step.
Notify listeners outside the state lock and record listener failures. The reference callbacks are synchronous; use an asynchronous queue if notification must not delay the caller.
Safe when many workers update steps at once.

entities.name: StepState
entities.role: Enum of states: pending, running, retrying, succeeded, failed, cancelled.

entities.name: Transition
entities.role: Immutable record of one change.

entities.name: TransitionPolicy
entities.role: Which moves are legal; swappable.

entities.name: InMemoryTransitionStore
entities.role: Append-only history per workflow and step; swappable for a database.

entities.name: TransitionListener
entities.role: Anything that wants to react to a change.

entities.name: WorkflowStepLogger
entities.role: Facade that validates, stores, and notifies.

interfaces: record(workflow_id, step_id, to_state, actor, reason): validate and append; returns the Transition.
history(workflow_id, step_id): a copy of every transition, oldest first.
current_state(workflow_id, step_id): latest state, or None if never seen.
subscribe(listener): listener.on_transition(t) is called after each record; notification_failures records failed callbacks without undoing the transition.
concurrency: Reading the current state and appending must happen under one lock, or two workers can both start the same step.
Listeners run outside the lock so a slow one cannot block writers.
One global lock is the simple start; per-key locks or a database row lock scale further.
Transitions are immutable, so they are safe to share across threads.
extensions: Persist to a database with a unique constraint on (workflow, step, sequence).
Add idempotency keys so a retried worker call does not double-log.
Emit transitions as OpenTelemetry events for tracing.
Support per-workflow custom policies.

bugs.bug: Reads the current state, then appends, with no lock. Two workers can both move PENDING to RUNNING.
bugs.fix: Do the read, check, and append under one lock.

bugs.bug: No RETRYING or CANCELLED, and FAILED can go back to RUNNING silently. SUCCEEDED has no entry, so any move from it raises KeyError instead of a clear error.
bugs.fix: Model every state, make terminal states explicit, and add RETRYING.

bugs.bug: The logger sends email over SMTP inside record(). Logging now blocks on the network, and an SMTP failure raises after the event was already stored.
bugs.fix: Move notifications to a listener (Observer) called after the write, isolated from failures.

bugs.bug: Returns the internal list, and history is a public dict, so callers can change the log.
bugs.fix: Return a copy and keep storage private.

bugs.bug: Unknown workflow or step raises KeyError.
bugs.fix: Return None and an empty list for unknown keys.

bugs.bug: datetime.now() is naive local time, so timestamps are ambiguous across hosts.
bugs.fix: Use timezone-aware UTC from an injectable clock.

problems.title: Incident ticket state machine
requirements: Incidents move open, acknowledged, mitigated, resolved, closed.
Guards: acknowledge needs an owner; closing a SEV1 or SEV2 needs an RCA link.
Resolved incidents can be reopened; closed is final.
Keep a timeline of every change; failed attempts leave no trace.

entities.name: Status
entities.role: Enum of incident states.

entities.name: Event
entities.role: Enum of actions: ack, mitigate, resolve, reopen, close.

entities.name: Incident
entities.role: The ticket: severity, owner, RCA link, timeline.

entities.name: IncidentStateMachine
entities.role: Transition table plus guards; the only thing that changes status.

problems.diagram:
classDiagram
  class Incident {
    id
    severity
    status
    assignee
    rca_link
    timeline
  }
  class IncidentStateMachine {
    +fire(incident, event, actor) Status
    +allowed_events(incident) list
  }
  class Status {
    OPEN
    ACKNOWLEDGED
    MITIGATED
    RESOLVED
    CLOSED
  }
  IncidentStateMachine --> Incident : changes
  Incident --> Status
interfaces: fire(incident, event, actor): apply an event if the table and guards allow; returns the new status.
allowed_events(incident): events with a transition from the current status; guard checks still run in fire(), so a listed event may require an owner or RCA link.
concurrency: Validate and apply under one lock so two responders cannot both acknowledge.
In a real system use optimistic concurrency: a version number checked on update.
extensions: Escalation timers: auto-page the next level if not acknowledged in N minutes.
Severity changes as their own events with audit.
Persist the timeline and emit events to a bus.

bugs.bug: Appends to the timeline before validating, so rejected transitions still appear in the history.
bugs.fix: Validate first, then apply and record.

bugs.bug: No guards: acknowledge without an owner and close a SEV1 without an RCA are allowed.
bugs.fix: Add guard functions per transition.

bugs.bug: CLOSED can go back to OPEN, so closed is not final, and OPEN can jump straight to RESOLVED with no acknowledgement.
bugs.fix: Make CLOSED terminal and reopen only from RESOLVED.

bugs.bug: Status is a public attribute, so any code can set it and skip every rule.
bugs.fix: Only the state machine changes status.

bugs.bug: No lock: concurrent transitions can interleave.
bugs.fix: Lock, or use a version check on update.

bugs.bug: Plain strings: a typo like Resolved becomes a KeyError at runtime.
bugs.fix: Use Enums.

problems.title: Rate limiter: token bucket and sliding window
requirements: Limit requests per key: tenant, user, or API key.
Token bucket allows bursts up to capacity; sliding window enforces an exact count per window.
Use one allow interface for whole-request costs. TokenBucket also supports positive fractional cost; SlidingWindowLog rejects fractional request counts.
Thread-safe and testable with a fake clock. Each sliding window is bounded by its limit; the registry grows with distinct keys and needs an eviction policy for unbounded tenants.

entities.name: RateLimiter
entities.role: Interface: allow(cost) returns True or False.

entities.name: TokenBucket
entities.role: Refills continuously; caps at capacity.

entities.name: SlidingWindowLog
entities.role: Keeps recent timestamps; evicts old ones.

entities.name: RateLimiterRegistry
entities.role: One limiter per key, created on first use.

interfaces: allow(cost=1): True if the request may proceed. Cost must be positive and finite; the token bucket supports fractional cost, while the sliding request log requires whole counts.
RateLimiterRegistry.allow(key, cost): looks up or creates the limiter for a key.
concurrency: Refill and take must be one atomic step per bucket.
Creating a limiter for a new key must be atomic, or two threads build two buckets.
Use a monotonic clock; wall clocks can jump backwards.
Across many servers, move the state to Redis with a Lua script (see the system design page).
extensions: Distributed version on Redis.
Per-endpoint limits and plans.
Return Retry-After from the bucket's refill time.
Evict idle keys from the registry.

bugs.bug: int(now - last) drops fractions of a second, and last still moves to now, so a client calling every 0.9 seconds never refills.
bugs.fix: Refill with the exact elapsed time as a float.

bugs.bug: Tokens are never capped at capacity, so after a long idle period a client gets an unlimited burst.
bugs.fix: tokens = min(capacity, tokens + elapsed * rate).

bugs.bug: No locks: concurrent requests can overspend tokens, and the global limiters dict can create two buckets for one key.
bugs.fix: Lock each bucket and the registry.

bugs.bug: Old timestamps are never removed, so memory grows forever and every call scans the full history.
bugs.fix: Evict timestamps older than the window with a deque.

bugs.bug: Hard-coded wall clock: untestable and wrong when the clock jumps.
bugs.fix: Inject a monotonic clock.

problems.title: Job scheduler with retries
requirements: Run jobs at or after a scheduled time.
Retry failures with exponential backoff and jitter, up to a limit.
Jobs that keep failing go to a dead-letter list for a human.
Submitting the same job twice is a no-op.
Deterministic tests with a fake clock.

entities.name: Job
entities.role: Function, run time, attempts, last error.

entities.name: _Entry
entities.role: Heap entry ordered by time and sequence, never by Job.

entities.name: JobScheduler
entities.role: Heap of pending jobs, retry policy, dead letters.

problems.diagram:
classDiagram
  class JobScheduler {
    +submit(job_id, fn, delay, max_retries) bool
    +run_pending() int
    dead_letters
  }
  class Job {
    id
    run_at
    attempts
    max_retries
    last_error
  }
  JobScheduler o-- Job
interfaces: submit(job_id, fn, delay, max_retries): schedule once; False if the id already exists.
run_pending(): run every due job; returns the count.
dead_letters: jobs that exhausted their retries, with the last error.
concurrency: Pop jobs under the lock, run them outside it, so a slow job does not block submits.
With multiple workers, each popped job is owned by one worker; in a database, use a lease with a timeout.
Retries must be idempotent; the job id doubles as the idempotency key.
extensions: Persist jobs so a restart does not lose them.
Leases and heartbeats for multiple workers.
Cron schedules.
Per-job timeouts.

bugs.bug: Entries are (run_at, Job). When two jobs share a run_at, Python compares Job objects and raises TypeError.
bugs.fix: Add a sequence number tiebreak before the job.

bugs.bug: No retry limit and no dead letters: a job that always fails retries forever.
bugs.fix: Add max_retries and a dead-letter list.

bugs.bug: Failed jobs are re-queued at time.time(), so they retry immediately in a hot loop, run_pending may never return, and the failing dependency gets hammered.
bugs.fix: Exponential backoff with jitter.

bugs.bug: No lock around the shared heap.
bugs.fix: Lock heap operations; run jobs outside the lock.

bugs.bug: No idempotency: submitting the same job twice runs it twice.
bugs.fix: Track known ids.

bugs.bug: The error is swallowed with no record, so nobody can see why jobs fail.
bugs.fix: Store the last error and log it.

problems.title: LRU cache with TTL
requirements: Bounded size; evict the least recently used entry.
Entries expire after a TTL; expired entries are never returned.
Reads count as use; overwriting a key does not grow the cache.
A stored None is different from a miss.

entities.name: LRUTTLCache
entities.role: OrderedDict of key to (value, expires_at), plus a lock and clock.

problems.diagram:
classDiagram
  class LRUTTLCache {
    capacity
    ttl
    +get(key, default) value
    +put(key, value, ttl)
    -evict()
  }
interfaces: get(key, default=None): value if present and fresh, else default.
put(key, value, ttl=None): insert or overwrite; evicts expired first, then LRU.
concurrency: A read changes recency, so get needs the lock too.
One lock is fine in-process; for hot caches, shard into N caches by key hash.
extensions: Background sweeper for expired entries.
Size in bytes instead of entry count.
Write-through to a backing store.
Hit-rate metrics.

bugs.bug: TTL is stored but never checked, so expired values are returned.
bugs.fix: Compare expiry to the clock on read.

bugs.bug: Reads do not update recency, so this is FIFO, not LRU.
bugs.fix: Move the key to the most-recent end on read.

bugs.bug: Overwriting an existing key in a full cache evicts a different key, and the key is appended to the order list twice.
bugs.fix: Handle existing keys before checking capacity.

bugs.bug: O(n) eviction on a list.
bugs.fix: OrderedDict or a dict plus doubly linked list.

bugs.bug: No lock; data and order can drift apart under concurrency.
bugs.fix: Lock both operations.

bugs.bug: Returns None for both a miss and a stored None.
bugs.fix: Use a sentinel or a default argument.

problems.title: In-memory pub/sub bus
requirements: Subscribe handlers to topics; publish delivers to every current subscriber.
Subscribing returns a handle used to unsubscribe.
A failing handler must not stop delivery to others; record the failure so delivery can be inspected or retried.
Handlers may subscribe, unsubscribe, or publish while being called.

entities.name: Subscription
entities.role: Handle with topic and id.

entities.name: PubSubBus
entities.role: Topic to handlers map, lock, dead letters.

interfaces: subscribe(topic, handler): returns a Subscription handle.
unsubscribe(sub): True if it was active.
publish(topic, message): delivers to a snapshot of subscribers; returns how many succeeded.
concurrency: Copy the subscriber list under the lock, deliver outside it.
Holding a non-reentrant lock while calling handlers deadlocks if a handler publishes.
Isolate each handler's exceptions.
extensions: Async delivery with a queue per subscriber.
Wildcard topics.
Retries and a dead-letter topic.
Backpressure when a subscriber falls behind.

bugs.bug: Publishing to a topic with no subscribers raises KeyError.
bugs.fix: Use .get(topic, {}).

bugs.bug: One handler's exception stops delivery to every handler after it.
bugs.fix: Catch per handler and record to dead letters.

bugs.bug: Holds a non-reentrant lock while calling handlers, so a handler that publishes deadlocks.
bugs.fix: Snapshot under the lock, deliver outside it.

bugs.bug: Lists change without the lock while publish iterates; a handler that unsubscribes itself makes the loop skip the next handler.
bugs.fix: Lock mutations and iterate over a copy.

bugs.bug: Needs the same function object, so lambdas cannot be unsubscribed, and subscribe returns nothing.
bugs.fix: Return a Subscription handle.

problems.title: Alert deduplicator
requirements: Page once per real problem; suppress repeats within a window.
Ignore labels that change every firing, like pod or timestamp.
Always page on escalation to a worse severity.
Page again after the window, or after the alert resolves and fires again.
Memory stays bounded.

entities.name: Alert
entities.role: Service, name, severity, labels.

entities.name: _Group
entities.role: First seen, last paged, worst severity, count.

entities.name: AlertDeduplicator
entities.role: Fingerprint to group map with a window and clock.

problems.diagram:
classDiagram
  class AlertDeduplicator {
    window_s
    +fingerprint(alert) str
    +ingest(alert) str
    +resolve(alert) bool
    +count(alert) int
  }
  class Alert {
    service
    name
    severity
    labels
  }
  AlertDeduplicator --> Alert : groups
interfaces: ingest(alert): returns the fingerprint if it should page, None if suppressed.
resolve(alert): clears the group so the next firing pages.
fingerprint(alert): stable hash of service, name, and meaningful labels.
concurrency: Read, decide, and update a group under one lock, or two replicas of the same alert both page.
Across several dedup instances, shard by fingerprint or use a shared store with atomic updates.
extensions: Group related fingerprints into one incident.
Per-team windows.
Flapping detection.
Persist groups across restarts.

bugs.bug: Includes every label, including pod and timestamp, so repeats of the same problem never match.
bugs.fix: Drop volatile labels and sort the rest.

bugs.bug: No window: once seen, an alert is suppressed forever.
bugs.fix: Re-page after the window passes.

bugs.bug: Escalation is suppressed: a SEV1 after a SEV2 never pages.
bugs.fix: Always page when severity gets worse.

bugs.bug: No resolve and no cleanup, so memory grows forever and a resolved alert that fires again stays silent.
bugs.fix: Add resolve() and expire stale groups.

bugs.bug: No lock: the check and insert race, so duplicates can both page.
bugs.fix: Lock the read-decide-update.
